desc: a '{' inside a string opens interpolation; the expression references a field
exercise:
field Name as string
field Greeting as string <- "Hello {Name}"

desc: '{{' is the escape for a literal open brace inside a string
exercise: field Note as string default "a {{ b"

desc: '}}' is the escape for a literal close brace inside a string
exercise: field Note as string default "a }} b"

desc: "{}" is lexically valid but the parser rejects empty interpolation (expected expression)
recognized string escapes \" \\ \n \t are accepted
a single-quoted typed constant with no interpolation is a single TypedConstant; type from context
recognized typed-constant escapes include \' and \\
exercise:
field S as string
field T as string <- 'it\'s'

desc: \n is NOT a valid typed-constant escape (unlike in strings)
\t is NOT a valid typed-constant escape
content words like 'days' inside a typed constant are not language keywords; validated by type checker
exercise: field Grace as duration default '3 days'

desc: content words like 'USD' inside a typed constant are not keywords
exercise: field Price as money default '10 USD'

desc: a list literal [1, 2, 3] tokenizes as bracket/number/comma punctuation assembled by the parser
exercise: field Levels as choice of integer(1, 2, 3)

desc: a list literal ["a", "b"] tokenizes with string literals
exercise: field Tags as choice of string("a", "b")

desc: a '#' begins a comment to end of line; a standalone comment line is trivia
exercise:
# a comment
field Balance as number

desc: a '#' comment may follow code on the same line
exercise: field Balance as number  # inline comment

desc: leading indentation is cosmetic; it does not change meaning
exercise:
field A as number
    field B as number

desc: a declaration may span multiple lines freely; newlines are trivia, keywords are the boundaries
'<-' scans as BackArrow (computed-field arrow), not '<' followed by '-'
exercise:
field A as number
field B as number <- A + 1

desc: '->' scans as Arrow (action-chain / outcome separator)
exercise: from Draft on Submit -> set A = 0 -> transition Approved

desc: '~=' is case-insensitive equals, valid on string operands
exercise:
field A as string
field B as string
rule R: A ~= B because "ci compare"

desc: '~=' is string-only; applying it to numeric operands is a type error
exercise:
field A as number
field B as number
rule R: A ~= B because "bad"

desc: '!~' is case-insensitive not-equals, string-only
exercise:
field A as string
field B as string
rule R: A !~ B because "ci compare"

desc: '~' before 'string' is the case-insensitive scalar field type qualifier
'~' before a non-string type is invalid (caught by parser/type checker)
'~startsWith' lexes as Tilde + identifier 'startsWith'; parser recognizes it as a CI function call
exercise:
field Name as string
rule R: ~startsWith(Name, "A") because "ci prefix"

desc: Tilde in prefix position before an identifier other than startsWith/endsWith emits ExpectedToken
exercise:
field Name as string
rule R: ~contains(Name, "A") because "bad"

desc: '~' before a collection inner type marks case-insensitive inner (set of ~string)
'set' after 'of'/'as' is reinterpreted as SetType (collection type)
exercise: field Tags as set of string

desc: 'set' after '->' is the Set action keyword
exercise: from Draft on Go -> set Balance = 0 -> transition Done

desc: 'is set' composes from separate Is + Set tokens as a presence operator on optional fields
exercise:
field Note as string optional
rule R: Note is set because "must be present"

desc: 'min' followed by a number literal is the constraint keyword
exercise: field Score as number min 0 max 100

desc: 'min' followed by '(' is the built-in function call
exercise:
field A as number
field B as number
field C as number <- min(A, B)

desc: 'max' followed by '(' is the built-in function call
exercise:
field A as number
field B as number
field C as number <- max(A, B)

desc: 'in' after a state name is a routing/scoping preposition
exercise:
field Amount as number
in Draft ensure Amount > 0 because "positive in draft"

desc: 'in' after a domain type is a unit type-qualifier
'of' after a collection keyword is the collection inner type qualifier
exercise: field Tags as set of string

desc: 'of' after a domain type is a dimension-family qualifier
a field may use 'in' or 'of' but not both (except price's two axes)
exercise: field Amount as money in 'USD' of 'length'
